checks.what: russian-federation gain Dec 1991 from the RSFSR of region Chukotka (2,485 cells, about 628,000 km2 against the page's 721,481-737,700 km2; 401 cells lie east of 180, lon -179.97 to -169.91, lat 64.3-71.5; no St Lawrence Island or Diomede cells). Page: 'Chukotka ... is the easternmost federal subject of Russia'; 'the only part of Russia lying partially in the Western Hemisphere'; 'In 1991, Chukotka declared its separation to become a subject of the Russian Federation in its own right'. The Dec 1991 date is the Federation's own founding (dossier), not a claim from the page. Trial stage: the 401 eastern cells go RSFSR -> russian-federation in 1991 by this event and stay Russian through 1999 and in the p2000 anchor; the published draft had them ownerless 1991-1999 after RSFSR ledger/67.

south-africa gain Apr 1994 from nobody of Transkei (132) + Venda (30) + Ciskei (39) = 201 cells, exactly the cells the dossier's vassal_end events ledger/13, /15, /16 sent to null in the published draft. Page: Bantustans 'were dismantled and their territories reincorporated into the Republic of South Africa with effect from 27 April 1994'; table gives Transkei 1976-1994, Venda 1979-1994, Ciskei 1981-1994. Trial stage: the 201 cells stay south-africa, status direct from 1994 to 1999 and in the p2000 anchor (published: nobody 1994-1999).

belize gain 1990 from british-colonial-empire of country Belize (84 cells, about 21,244 km2 against the page's 22,970 km2). Page: 'Belize achieved its independence from the United Kingdom on 21 September 1981'. The 1990 date is an in-window repair, not a historical date, and the note says so. Trial stage: 74 cells go BCE -> belize in 1990, Belize holds all 84 through 1999 and in the p2000 anchor, and the BCE 1996 snap now removes 11 cells instead of 85. Root cause lies earlier: in the published p1980-p1989 draft the british-colonial-empire_1984 snap takes the 74 cells from Belize in 1984, so 1984-1989 and 1 Jan 1990 are still wrong (see problems).

revolutionary-united-front_1993: the dossier's 3-cell border band (99 cells) minus country Liberia = 47 cells on the Sierra Leone side. Page: in March 1993 the SLA 'pushed the RUF to the Sierra Leone - Liberia border'; 'By the end of 1993 ... pushing the RUF rebels back to the Liberian border'; Liberian gains 'were restricting the ability of Charles Taylor's NPFL to trade with the RUF'. No RUF land inside Liberia on the page. Trial stage: the 52 band cells inside Liberia keep their earlier owners (republic-of-liberia 44, nobody 6, sierra-leone 2) in 1993-1999 instead of going to the RUF; RUF's Sierra Leone holdings unchanged (47 cells in 1993).

revolutionary-united-front_1994 (1994-2001): the dossier's own union of Eastern Province (76 cells) and the border band, with only the Liberian part of the band cut. The page has no 1994 sentence, but the entry changes nothing the dossier did not already claim except removing Liberian land the page never gives the RUF. Trial stage: RUF holds 91 Sierra Leonean cells 1994-1999, identical to the published draft; Liberia keeps its 44 cells. The keyframe runs to 2001, so the cut also acts in the p2000-p2009 window (reported by the window agent).

russian-federation_1991: base spec identical to the dossier's correction (cliopatria Russian Federation 1992), plus region Chukotka. Page supports Chukotka as Russian and partly in the Western Hemisphere. Trial: snap 1991 'kept by others' drops from 13 to 6; Chukotka east of 180 stays Russian.

russian-federation_1992: base spec identical to the dossier's correction (cliopatria 1992), plus Chukotka. Without it the 1992 snap would drop the 401 eastern cells again. Trial: the 1992 snap removes 149 instead of 151 cells and the 401 Chukotka cells stay Russian 1992-1994.
russian-federation_1995 (1995-1996): base spec identical to the dossier's correction (cliopatria 1996), plus Chukotka. Trial: Chukotka east of 180 Russian in 1995-1996.

russian-federation_1996: base spec identical to the dossier's correction (cliopatria 1996 minus Chechen Republic 1992), plus Chukotka. Trial: Chukotka east of 180 Russian 1997-1999 and in the p2000 anchor (412 cells nobody -> russian-federation against the published anchor: 401 Chukotka + 11 border cells). The 2000/2006/2014/2024 keyframes still lack it (window agent's dossier request).

Poland wins over the Byelorussian SSR 1990-1991, no region. The conflict is 101 cells in 1990 (republic-of-poland_1990 keyframe), all inside country Poland: 88 Podlaskie, 13 Lubelskie; none in Belarus. Bialystok page: 'On 20 September 1944 the city was transferred back to Poland' and became 'capital of the initial Bialystok Voivodeship of the People's Republic of Poland'. I also opened Belarus-Poland border: Bialystok and 3 districts 'were restored to Poland' under the agreement of 16 August 1945, last change by the treaty of 15 May 1948, and 'Thereafter, and until now, the border between Poland and Belarus has never changed', which covers the 13 Lublin cells. Trial: the ruling settles 101 cell-years; the cells go to Poland in 1990 instead of BSSR 1990 and nobody 1991; the 1992 Poland snap no longer has to move 102 cells. 1 Jan 1990 still shows BSSR on 107 Polish cells (earlier windows).

USSR wins over empire-of-japan 1990-1991, no region. The conflict cells are 7: three on South Sakhalin (46.7N 142.5-143.1E), one on the Terpeniya coast of Sakhalin (48.9N 144.6E) and three on Iturup (44.6-45.3N 147.1-148.0E). Page: 'The disputed islands are under Russian administration as the South Kuril District'; the Japanese inhabitants 'were expelled'; at San Francisco in 1951 Japan renounced 'that portion of Sakhalin and the islands adjacent to it'; Japan's present claim covers the four southern islands only. Trial: the 7 cells go Japan -> USSR in 1990 and -> russian-federation in 1991 (R2), and no Japan/Russia conflict is left in 1991-1999 (published: 35 cell-years to Japan). Not drawing Japan's dormant claim as a contest is a defensible choice.

problems: Missed by the window agent: empire-of-japan holds two Liaodong cells, 206821 (39.38N 122.36E) and 206892 (39.03N 121.49E), from the 1990 anchor through 1999 and in the p2000 anchor. The size rule beats the PRC keyframes of 1992, 1997 and 1999. Fix: a ruling for people-s-republic-of-china over empire-of-japan, years 1990-1999, with a page on the return of the Kwantung Leased Territory to China. The root is in earlier windows.

Belize root cause is earlier: in the published p1980-p1989 draft the british-colonial-empire_1984 snap (keyframe_cells 374) moves 74 cells of Belize to the BCE in 1984. Yet the dossier's british-colonial-empire_1984 correction subtracts country Belize, and the gazetteer resolves that correction to 83 cells with 0 in Belize. So the compile's keyframe shape and the gazetteer disagree, and the coordinator should look at it. 1984-1989 and 1 Jan 1990 still show Belize as a British colony. events/2 only repairs it from 1990.

Cross-boundary, as the window agent reported: keyframe_overrides/1 acts through 2001. Chukotka east of 180 will be snapped away again by russian-federation_2000/_2006/_2014/_2024 unless the p2000+ windows patch the same way or the dossier changes.

Unflagged slop: when the RSFSR ends (ledger/67) about 290 cells go to nobody and are still ownerless in the stage p2000 anchor. Of these, 82 are Ladoga, Onega and Peipus lake cells. The others are mostly lake and shore cells near Baikal and Karelia, about 20 Arctic island or coast cells north of 78N, and a few on the Caspian and Black Sea coasts. Nobody's lakes may be the project convention; the Arctic cells are probably Russian land.

Start anchor p1990 still has the BSSR holding 107 Polish cells and the BCE holding 74 Belize cells on 1 January 1990, and only 47 of the bantustan cells carry a vassal tint. All three come from earlier windows.
